text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD

- Wim Duisenberg, the departing president of the Dutch central bank and mooted first president of the the planned European Central bank, says in interview admission criteria for EMU should not be interpreted in a "bookkeeper like" way. (p1)
- Consumer spending over the first four months of 1997 was up three percent over the same period in 1996, according to Dutch government statistics (p7)
- Computer company Tulip of Den Bosch buys Dutch competitor Commodore BV. Company expects the deal to provide synergies. (p3).
- Dutch PTT has been told to lower the prices it will charge competitors for access to its national network. (p1)
- Hoogovens has no plans to split itself into separate steel and aluminium bourse listed units (p1)

- The Netherlands would be the world's second most wealthy nation, behind the U.S., if Dutch employees increased the number of hours they worked to be in line with other countries according to research for U.S. employers' organisation (p1)
VOLKSKRANT
- Household goods retailer Blokker must sell off the nine Toys 'R Us shops it bought last year, European Commission rules (p1)
- Software company ICT ends first day on bourse at 27.20
guilders, up from the issue price of 26 guilderes. (p15)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Subscriptions for retail investment in the offering of Prolion shares closed on Thursday, earlier than the planned closure on Monday. Institutional applications still open (p23)
- Issuers of electronic cash payment cards Chipper and Chipknip are about to go on the offensive in coming months (p25)
- ICT share offer around 30 times oversubscribed. (p25)

- Demand for personnel to staff "call centres" -- where consumer queries can be dealt with on the phone -- is set to soar to as high as 120,000 by 2000 from a current 25,000, according to a management consultants survey. (p25)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Berlo Service Group, a business that repairs Philips made appliances, is bankrupt with the loss of 250 jobs. (p13)
